change: Follow docs/v3/EXPRESSION.md § The loop for cases n11, n22, n23, n24, n25 and n26 (all native; none has run). Before pinning, check TuffUI (github.com/yurigdesigner/tuffui) for visualization components published after `f31ea2b` (2026-11-16; cycle 6 found Model Picker, run as c16, and Voice Session, a call control and no visualization); for each one, add a `c` case, its reference row and shot (`.evidence/v3-shots/expression-6/ref-shot.ts` in the main checkout shoots a page at 1440x1000 with reduced motion), and run it in place of a native case. With fewer than four referenced cases the cycle file reports the convergence clause on the referenced cases it has and says the clause cannot be met in full; with none, the verdict counts are empty. You are the lead: you spawn, shoot, collect and diagnose; you build nothing and score nothing. (1) Builders: one fresh subagent per case on the default worker tier, with the case row verbatim, the scenario id `expr-<case id>`, and the fence of cycle 6 (its builder prompt, `.evidence/v3-shots/expression-6/builder-prompt.md` in the main checkout, is the model). Pre-register the registry and scenario-info entries with placeholders so each builder owns one directory, run oxfmt on scenario-info.ts after adding them, and tell builders that `fixture` reaches the scenario as a prop. Each builder builds into its own dist directory and shoots its own route. (2) Shoot each scenario with apps/playground/scripts/shots.ts, plus the keyboard frame, the list frame and the pointer sweep of cycle 6's lead tool (`.evidence/v3-shots/expression-6/lead-shots.ts`, with its `shoot-round.sh`: its list frame now logs whether the row linked on the stepped path or only on direct arrival). (3) Reviewers: one fresh subagent per case and round, never the builder, with the case row, the shot paths, a snapshot of the scenario source for that round, docs/v3/expression/rubric.md and the shoot log. Tell it to open every shot. (4) Repair: hand the builder its reviewer's findings, at most two more rounds, shooting and scoring after each. (5) Diagnose every point lost in round 0 into one class from EXPRESSION.md § Finding classes, using the builder's wish list and its workaround comments as evidence. Where an open plan row already owns a gap, class the finding `planned` and append it as a `notes` entry to that row's brief instead of filing a row. (6) Judge the three hypotheses against EXPRESSION.md § Thresholds, using this cycle's numbers and the verdict lines of docs/v3/spikes/viz-census.md. (7) File per CYCLES.md step 6. A fix that adds a public export, changes charts/contract.ts or changes what primitive-bypass denies is one row with `checkpoint: spec` and seat opus high. Report factory friction with `factory signal file`, not as a row. Lead notes from cycle 6: (a) check v3-expr-6-kit-fixes (1) to (3) before round 0 with `.evidence/v3-shots/expression-6/probe-steps.ts` on c16's scenario (a pointer crossing the chart onto a table row keeps its focus), n15's keys log (one announcement per move) and n21 at 390 (its median label shows); if any did not land, tell builders so the same gap does not cost twice; (b) check v3-expr-6-contract: if its fields have not shipped, tell reviewers a conditional spread for a maybe-absent prop is the known form, and count it as glue, not as a defect; (c) run `make check-fast` before scoring round 0, and stop it by pid before builders start round 1 only if it is still queued for a slot; check-contract-frozen compares against `origin/master`, so a master that moved past the pin reports pin changes this tree did not make: name it, do not chase it; (d) tell reviewers what cycle 6's reviewer prompt says about the two sanctioned colour forms, the 61 px band (`page.tsx:146`) and the LIST approach; (e) count whether builders shoot a keyboard frame unasked once v3-expr-6-skill (10) lands (cycle 5: 0 of 6, cycle 6: 0 of 6); (f) once this cycle runs, the bank's only never-run cases are n27 and the ones it adds: add at least five from pages no case covers yet, so cycle 8 can draw six, and say so; (g) report every score on all items and, for the trend against cycles 1 and 2, on the F and K items alone, as cycles 3 to 6 do.
